module


public import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Finset.Nat
public import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card

@[expose] public section

@[simp]
theorem Nat.ncard_Iio (b : ℕ) : (Set.Iio b).ncard = b := by
  rw [← Finset.coe_Iio, Set.ncard_coe_finset]
  exact Nat.card_Iio _

findings.description: The theorem at lines 25–27 exactly duplicates Mathlib's existing `Set.ncard_Iio_nat`. Both are `[simp]` lemmas with type `∀ b : ℕ, (Set.Iio b).ncard = b`. The mathematics is correct; this is only duplication of an existing Mathlib declaration.
findings.source_evidence: The checked-out Mathlib file `Mathlib/Order/Interval/Set/Nat.lean`, lines 40–41, already states, inside namespace `Set`: `@[simp] lemma ncard_Iio_nat (b : ℕ) : (Iio b).ncard = b`. Lean `#check` confirmed that both declarations have identical types.
findings.suggested_fix: Import `Mathlib.Order.Interval.Set.Nat` and use `Set.ncard_Iio_nat` at the existing use sites. Remove the duplicate theorem, or retain its old name as a deprecated compatibility alias if needed.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization found. This file contains only the one proved lemma and introduces no definitions. Lean experiments in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` confirmed that `Set.Iio b` is finite for every natural b, equals the coercion of `Finset.range b`, and has the correct empty and smallest nonempty cases. Its cardinality therefore never uses the infinite-set default value of ncard. The proof has no sorry dependency. Computations and proofs in `/workspace/review/use_sites.lean` checked the interval normalization used by Nat.hasDensity_even and Erdos786.erdos_786.parts.i.example, including the zero-denominator boundary, which lies outside the positive tail used for convergence. The external Erdős source confirms the density-1/4 example and still records the distinct-factor questions as open. Both scratch files compile without errors or warnings; the checkout was left unchanged.
